paragraphs.text: DSH Plugin-based AI Web Novel Writer, and Skill
# ai-novelist
English | 中文

A **DSH plugin** that turns DeepSeek Harness into an AI web-novel composer — and, more
precisely, in

to an executable copy of a web-novel production SOP. The agent gets a real
project file, a planning

pipeline with gates, a story bible, a per-chapter contract, a
metric ledger calibrated against same-

genre medians, and a manuscript exporter — instead
of holding a novel in its context window.
Built for @deepseek-ai/dsh `0.2.0-rc.2`.
## What it adds

**Nine model-facing tools**, one per capability, matching the phases of the SOP
(see The SOP this im

plements below) — plus one that
deliberately sits outside them. Eight of them
**compute** — threshol

ds, gates, arithmetic, identical on every run. The ninth,
`novel_review`, **asks a model** to judge

prose, because that is the one thing no
counter can decide; it is registered only where a model rout

cause that is the one thing no
counter can decide; it is registered only where a model route exists.

Two of the nine exist because a pipeline that runs from an inspiration straight to
chapters is a pip

eline that never asked the author anything. `novel_confirm` records
the checkpoints only the author

can close — the **settings** sign-off, which must
exist before chapter 1 and is itself settled one l

ayer at a time (立意 → 世界观 →
人物设定 → 全书大纲 → 分卷大纲), and the **文风复核** of the prose voice, due once the
go

lden three chapters (第 1–3 章) have prose and before chapter 4. Two things gate the
prose: the premis

e, and the 写作风格 block of the 全书大纲 — seven named elements
written before chapter 1, because a voice c

hosen while writing the first chapter is a
voice the author never got to steer.
| Tool | SOP phase | What it owns |
| `novel_init` | 一 策划 | The project and its commercial frame — platform, mode (paid/free), audience,
genre, target readers, monetization — plus the calibration medians (`baselines`, same-genre metric
medians from the last 30 days) and the writing parameters: outline window, opening gate chapters, st
ock target, outline ceiling. The **length plan** (总字数, 单章字数, 是否分卷/分几卷) is asked of the user, never a
ssumed: unanswered questions come back as a checklist repeated every step, `totalChapters` is derive
d from total ÷ chapter length, and the numbers are cross-checked against each other and against the

volume outline. |
[该节后续省略]
### Writing craft (the "how it should read" half)

The SOP is good at deciding *what* must be planned and *what counts as a debt*. It cannot
teach *how

a hook lands, how a payoff is staged, or which sentence reads like a machine*.
That knowledge lives

in `docs/craft/` — fourteen authored sheets
(lane choice, trends, platform pacing, overseas, hooks,

payoffs, rhythm, naming, voice,
continuity, submission, fanfic, script, teaching) — and is availabl

e at runtime
without opening a file: `novel_status detail="craft"` lists them, and
`novel_status det

ail="craft" topic="hooks"` returns the sheet. The same Markdown is copied into
the skill distributio

n under `references/craft/`, so a skill-only install reads the same text.
The sheets deliberately do

**not** hard-code platform thresholds: they give the judgement and
tell you to check the platform's

current announcement, because a stale "签约门槛" is worse than
none.
## The SOP this implements

The workflow is `docs/sop.md` — 爆款网文创作全流程 SOP 3.9, whose closed loop
is **假设 → 验证 → 放大 → 复盘 → 复用**:

form a hypothesis from a competitor study and a
memorable point, put the opening package in front of

real readers, record a human go/no-go on
it, build the full skeleton only after a `go`, iterate whi

le serializing, then turn the
finished book into reusable structure.

Two axes, and only one of them is the pipeline. The **pipeline** — plan, opening package,
launch dec

ision, full skeleton, serial — advances on planned and written work alone; it never
waits for a plat

form number. The **data evaluation** (`novel_assess`) is started by the author
at the moment they as

k whether the book is still worth continuing, normally once the platform
has numbers to transcribe b

y hand; it is what turns readings into the 继续投入 / 换变量后继续
/ 切书止损 decision. Nothing gates on it: a pro

ject nobody has ever measured is a normal
project, and a missing reading is never a reason to stop.
The plugin's contribution is making that SOP *executable* rather than advisory:

- every step's output becomes a field in one project document, so nothing lives only in
prose and ge

ts forgotten;
[该节后续省略]
### What it will not do
Stated plainly, because the SOP is explicit that these are human or platform jobs:

- **It never invents a metric.** Numbers come from the platform, an editor, a test cohort,
or a huma

n's judgement. The tool records them, compares them with your baselines,
derives an action and a sco

pe, and warns. If nobody reports a reading, there is no
reading.
- **The eight computing tools never

judge prose.** The delivery report compares a draft with
the plan it was written against; the 去 AI

化 hints are countable statistics — paragraph
length, dialogue density, repeated sentence openings —

not a verdict on voice; and
compliance is a checklist you confirm rather than a scanner that reports

"clean".
`novel_review` *does* judge, which is why it is a separate tool with a separate record:
it

s findings cite the text, name the model and the rubric version, and enter no ledger a
threshold act

s on.
- **It never rewrites published chapters.** It records the intended scope of an iteration
and

reports promises that were due and not paid; the decision and the edit stay with the
author.
- **It
measures nothing by itself.** No platform API, no crawler, no analytics.
#### What "initialized" means, and how to undo it

Automatic initialization writes **only the empty scaffold**: `.novel/novel.json` with the
folder's n

ame as the title and every story field blank. Nothing you wrote is touched, nothing
is overwritten (

the write is `createIfAbsent`), and no story decision — premise, medians,
pitch, chapters — is inven

ted. That is the whole point: the scaffold is what makes the tools,
the prompt section and the Kanba

n board exist from your first message instead of waiting for
someone to remember `novel_init`.
If it claims a directory you did not mean, delete it and the composer forgets:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

To turn the eagerness down, set `workspaceMode: auto` (only marked projects are adopted) or
`off` (n
othing is ever written).
